primitives.name: Team-Aware Segmentation and Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper presents a lightweight Segment Anything Model (SAM)-based tracking approach for football player tracking: SAM with classical CSRT trackers enhanced by jersey color-based appearance models.

primitives.name: Appearance-Based Re-Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: We propose a team-aware tracking system that leverages SAM's precise segmentation for initialization and incorporates appearancebased re-identification using HSV color histograms extracted from jersey regions to improve occlusion recovery.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_i^t': 'HSV histogram of player i at time t (dimensionless)', 'd(H_i^t, H_j^t)': 'distance between HSV histograms (dimensionless)', 'R_{ij}': 're-identification confidence between players i and j (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Jersey colors remain consistent; HSV histograms capture sufficient discriminative features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When HSV histograms fail due to lighting variation or uniform similarity.

layer2.mapping: HSV histogram kernel defines similarity space for player re-identification in GSE's belief graph.
layer2.telemetry: Re-identification recovery rate, false match probability

primitives.name: Tracking Performance Evaluation Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our evaluation framework measures three key dimensions: processing speed (FPS and memory usage), tracking accuracy (success rate and bbox stability), and robustness (occlusion recovery rate and identity consistency).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{success}': 'tracking success rate (dimensionless)', 'F_{FPS}': 'frames per second (Hz)', 'M_{memory}': 'memory consumption (MB)', 'O_{recovery}': 'occlusion recovery rate (dimensionless)', 'I_{consistency}': 'identity consistency (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Evaluation metrics are independent and measurable across video sequences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When FPS drops below 5 Hz or memory exceeds 2 GB.

layer2.mapping: GSI's performance scoring aligns with empirical tracking metrics via Bayesian loss functions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core tracking architecture combines SAM’s segmentation precision with CSRT’s temporal coherence to form a hybrid tracking pipeline. In the initialization phase, SAM produces pixel-level masks that define player boundaries, which are then used as input to CSRT for motion prediction. Appearance models derived from HSV histograms enhance re-identification post-occlusion. The system operates under a dual constraint: minimizing computational overhead while maximizing tracking fidelity. Failure modes include occlusion beyond 50%, uniform appearance similarity, and extended off-screen periods. The trade-off between speed and accuracy manifests as a diminishing returns curve in FPS vs. identity consistency. The system's robustness hinges on the reliability of HSV histograms under illumination variance and the resilience of CSRT to motion blur. The evaluation framework quantifies this trade-off through FPS, memory, and success rate metrics, enabling deployment decisions based on resource constraints.
